display.title: The Four Chochmos, Part 1 (Shorter Version)
display.summary_short: A shorter recording of Part 1: after a talk on the Yomim Tovim of Kislev and trusting the Rebbe, Rabbi Yehuda saves four gold coins and sets off for the Leipzig fair.
display.summary_long: The storyteller begins with the special days of Kislev, the month of Geulah, from Rosh Chodesh Kislev and Tes Kislev, 'this Shabbos', through Yud-Tes Kislev and Chanukah. He explains that the Rebbe gives brachos even before we ask, and that we catch them with a good resolution. He tells how the Rebbe Rashab answered a bochur's doubting thought with 'I know who you are better than you know who you are', and how another Rebbe told a bochur who hid his forehead under his hat that he could see through the hat too. So we follow the Rebbe's advice, such as Chitas and Tehillim, even when it is hard. The story, which he first heard from his father, follows Rabbi Yehuda, whose guest room is fit for a king. To buy something special for his guests at the Leipzig fair, he puts aside a coin or two each day after giving tzedakah, and after a year changes four hundred small coins for four gold coins. Trusting Hashem, he gets a ride with his friend Reb Yankel and starts going from shop to shop. To be continued.
display.lesson: We cannot hide from a Rebbe; trust the tzaddik's advice and trust Hashem, who is in charge of success.

date.note: 'Vav Kislev, which was yesterday' and 'Tes Kislev, which is this Shabbos': a Thursday; year not stated.
